title: Lab 6 — Quiz 1
subtitle: Survey of Eukaryotes — fungi and protozoa

questions.prompt: Identify this fungus by its broom-shaped spore-forming structures.
questions.explanation: Penicillium: broom-shaped reproductive spore-forming structures; makes penicillin, causes food spoilage, not known to cause disease.

why.B: Candida appears as oval yeast cells or a mold form with pseudohyphae.

questions.prompt: Identify this fungus by its dandelion-shaped spore-forming structures (brightfield).
questions.explanation: Aspergillus: dandelion-shaped spore-forming structures. May cause farmer's lung, aspergillosis and systemic infections.

why.C: Candida is a dimorphic yeast/mold without dandelion heads.
why.D: Amoeba is a protozoan with pseudopods.

questions.prompt: These oval purple cells are a dimorphic fungus shown in its yeast form. Identify it.
questions.explanation: C. albicans is dimorphic: yeast form at 37°C, mold form at 25°C.

why.A: Aspergillus is a mold with dandelion-shaped heads.
why.C: Penicillium is a mold with broom-shaped structures.

questions.prompt: This specimen shows Candida albicans in its mold form. What does finding the mold form in a patient specimen suggest?

options.text: The infection is mild and will clear up without treatment
The infection is likely more severe, and stronger antifungal doses may be needed
The sample was contaminated by Penicillium from the air
The patient's body temperature must be above 37°C

questions.explanation: When Candida's mold form is visible in a patient specimen, the infection is likely more severe than with only the yeast form.

why.A: Mold form in a specimen points to a more severe infection.
why.C: This is Candida's own mold form (dimorphism).
why.D: The mold form grows at lower temperatures (25°C).

questions.prompt: Dimorphic fungi like Candida albicans grow in the yeast form at ___ and the mold form at ___.
questions.explanation: Yeast form at higher temperatures (37°C); mold form at lower temperatures (25°C).

why.A: Reversed: yeast at the higher temperature, mold at the lower.
why.B: The lower temperature is 25°C, not refrigeration.

questions.prompt: A white coating on a patient's tongue is HARD to scrape off with a tongue depressor. What does that suggest?

options.text: It might be an infection (oral thrush)

questions.explanation: Easy to scrape off → probably dried milk. Hard to scrape off → it might be an infection (oral thrush, Candida albicans).

why.C: Thrush is caused by Candida, a fungus.

questions.prompt: Most yeasts, like these cells, reproduce by:

why.A: Binary fission is how bacteria reproduce.
why.C: Spore structures belong to molds like Penicillium.
why.D: Cysts are formed by some protozoa.

questions.prompt: Identify this protozoan: common in the environment, non-pathogenic, moves using pseudopods.
questions.explanation: Amoeba proteus is non-pathogenic, but it can be mistaken for Acanthamoeba and Naegleria fowleri.

why.A: Entamoeba is an intestinal pathogen (amoebic dysentery).
why.C: Giardia is flagellated with a double nucleus.
why.D: Trichomonas is a flagellated STI protozoan.

questions.prompt: Identify these protozoan trophozoites, which have a double nucleus (the 'face').
questions.explanation: Giardia: double nucleus, flagellated; fecal-oral; fatty diarrhea ('beaver fever', 'hiker's diarrhea'); cysts and trophozoites.

why.C: Entamoeba is an amoeba without flagella.
why.D: Plasmodium appears as ring forms inside red blood cells.

questions.prompt: Identify this flagellated protozoan with a single nucleus per cell.
questions.explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis: sexually transmitted, trophozoite form only, single nucleus, flagellated, causes vaginitis.

why.B: Amoeba moves by pseudopods, not flagella.

questions.prompt: These ring forms are inside red blood cells. Identify the organism.
questions.explanation: Plasmodium: obligate intracellular parasite, visible as ring forms inside RBCs; causes malaria; mosquito vector.

why.A: Giardia lives in the intestine, not inside RBCs.
why.D: Candida is a yeast, not an RBC parasite.

questions.prompt: This organism transmits the cause of malaria. What is it?

options.text: A flea (transmits Taenia larvae to pets)

questions.explanation: Plasmodium is transmitted by a mosquito vector; it infects about 10% of the human population, with 300–500 million cases a year.

why.A: Fleas carry tapeworm larvae; malaria is spread by mosquitoes.

questions.prompt: Identify this intestinal amoeba that causes amoebic dysentery (bloody diarrhea).
questions.explanation: Entamoeba histolytica: intestinal, fecal-oral, amoebic dysentery, forms cysts and trophozoites.

why.B: Naegleria enters through the nose and infects the brain.

questions.prompt: Which amoeba infects the cornea, often when contact lenses are not cared for properly?
questions.explanation: Acanthamoeba may infect the cornea, often from poorly cared-for contact lenses.

why.A: Naegleria enters through the nose and travels to the brain.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Naegleria fowleri is FALSE?

options.text: It is spread by the fecal-oral route
It penetrates the nasal mucosa and travels to the brain
Very few people have survived infection

questions.explanation: Naegleria fowleri enters via the nose, not the fecal-oral route. Entamoeba and Giardia are fecal-oral.

why.B: True — it enters via the nose.
why.E: True — only 4 of 160+ US cases since the 1960s.
